v.q: Two threads call `put` on the same plain `HashMap` at the same time. What is the risk?
o: Lost updates or a corrupted internal structure
The second thread always throws an exception
The map sorts its entries automatically
v.w: `HashMap` is not thread-safe. Use `ConcurrentHashMap`, or confine the map to one thread.

v.q: Which statement about a plain HashMap used by several threads is NOT true?
o: It throws an exception on every concurrent put
It needs external synchronisation or a concurrent map
v.w: Failures are unpredictable: lost updates, wrong sizes or a corrupted structure, not a reliable exception.

v.q: Which statement about `ConcurrentHashMap` in Java 8+ is correct?
o: Writers lock only the affected bin, and reads do not lock at all
A single lock protects the whole map
Reads and writes both take the same global lock
It copies the whole table on every write
v.w: Empty bins are filled with CAS and occupied bins are locked individually. This lets many threads work in parallel.

v.q: Which operation on ConcurrentHashMap takes no lock?
v.w: Reads are lock-free. Writes lock only the affected bin.

v.q: Which code is a check-then-act race on a `ConcurrentHashMap`?
v.w: Each call is atomic, but two calls in a row are not. Use the single atomic methods instead.

v.q: Which call performs check-then-put as one atomic step?
v.w: putIfAbsent checks and inserts inside one atomic operation. The other combinations leave a gap between the steps.

o: So that `get` returning `null` always means the key is absent
Because null values would be slower to store
Because Java 8 removed null from collections
To save memory in each bin
v.w: In a concurrent map you cannot safely call `containsKey` afterwards to tell "absent" from "mapped to null", because another thread may change it in between.

v.q: What does map.get(key) returning null mean in a ConcurrentHashMap?
o: The key exists with a null value
v.w: Null values are rejected, so null can only mean absent. A HashMap cannot tell the two cases apart.

v.q: A list of event listeners is read thousands of times per second and changed once a day. Which collection suits it?
v.w: Reads take no lock and iterate a snapshot. Writes copy the whole array, which is fine when they are rare.

v.q: Which collection suits a queue with many writes and few reads?
v.w: CopyOnWriteArrayList copies the whole array on every write, so it is only good for rare changes.

v.q: A producer is faster than its consumers. How does a bounded `BlockingQueue` help?
o: `put` blocks when the queue is full, so the producer slows down
The queue drops the oldest items silently
The queue grows until memory is full
The queue converts itself into a topic
v.w: This is backpressure. An unbounded queue hides overload until the heap is exhausted.

v.q: Which statement about a bounded BlockingQueue is NOT true?
o: put drops the oldest item when full
put blocks when the queue is full
take blocks when it is empty
v.w: Blocking put makes the producer wait. Dropping would be an offer or overflow policy chosen explicitly.

v.q: Does iterating a `ConcurrentHashMap` while another thread modifies it throw `ConcurrentModificationException`?
o: No: its iterators are weakly consistent
Only when the map has more than 1,000 entries
v.w: Weakly consistent iterators keep going and may or may not reflect later changes. Plain collections use fail-fast iterators.

v.q: Which statement about ConcurrentHashMap iterators is NOT true?
o: They may or may not show later updates
v.w: Weakly consistent iterators tolerate changes. The fail-fast behaviour belongs to HashMap and ArrayList.

v.q: A shared request counter is updated by hundreds of threads. Why might `LongAdder` beat `AtomicLong`?
o: It spreads updates over several cells, so threads retry far less
It uses a global lock that is cheaper
It stores the counter in a database
It guarantees an exact snapshot on every read
v.w: Under contention many CAS attempts on one variable fail and retry. `LongAdder` sums its cells on read, which is not an atomic snapshot.

v.q: Which class counts events from hundreds of threads with the least contention?
v.w: LongAdder spreads updates over several cells and adds them up on read.
